title: Local essential surjectivity of a fully faithful map of stacks
statement: Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention] and a site $(\mathcal C,J)$ [def-weil-pbc-topos] small in the larger universe. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be categories fibred in groupoids on $\mathcal C$, with fibre groupoids in that universe. Assume both are $J$-stacks: isomorphism presheaves on slice sites are sheaves and every covering descent datum for objects is effective. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a functor over $\mathcal C$ compatible with pullback. Suppose each fibre functor $F_T$ is fully faithful, meaning that it induces a bijection on each isomorphism set. Then $F$ is an equivalence over $\mathcal C$ if and only if for every $T$ and $b\in\mathcal B(T)$ there is a $J$-covering of $T$ on which the restrictions of $b$ are isomorphic to images of objects of $\mathcal A$. An equivalence over $\mathcal C$ means a pullback-compatible inverse functor up to invertible natural transformations.

proof.text: If $F$ has an inverse over $\mathcal C$, its counit supplies, for every $b\in\mathcal B(T)$, an isomorphism $F(Gb)\cong b$ in the fibre over $T$. The identity covering of $T$ therefore gives the required local images.

Conversely fix $b\in\mathcal B(T)$ and choose a covering $(u_i:T_i\to T)$, objects $a_i\in\mathcal A(T_i)$ and isomorphisms $\phi_i:F(a_i)\cong b|_{T_i}$. For every common test object $V$ with maps $v_i:V\to T_i$, $v_j:V\to T_j$ satisfying $u_iv_i=u_jv_j$, fibrewise fullness and faithfulness give a unique isomorphism $\delta_{ij,V}:a_i|_V\to a_j|_V$ with $F(\delta_{ij,V})=(\phi_j|_V)^{-1}(\phi_i|_V)$. All expressions include the canonical pullback comparisons for $F$ and for iterated restrictions. Uniqueness makes these arrows compatible with further restrictions. On any common triple test object, cancellation gives $F(\delta_{jk}\delta_{ij})=\phi_k^{-1}\phi_i=F(\delta_{ik})$, so faithfulness gives the cocycle relation; similarly $\delta_{ii}=1$. Thus the $a_i$ form a covering descent datum. This formulation uses test objects, not the existence of fibre products in $\mathcal C$.

By the assumed effectiveness of every covering descent datum in $\mathcal A$, choose $a\in\mathcal A(T)$ with descent isomorphisms $\epsilon_i:a|_{T_i}\cong a_i$. Their compatibility is $\epsilon_j|_V=\delta_{ij,V}(\epsilon_i|_V)$ on every common test object $V$. This is exactly the given object-descent axiom, applied to the datum constructed in the preceding step.

Put $\theta_i=\phi_iF(\epsilon_i):F(a)|_{T_i}\cong b|_{T_i}$. On a common test object, $\theta_j=\phi_jF(\delta_{ij})F(\epsilon_i)=\phi_iF(\epsilon_i)=\theta_i$. By the assumed sheaf property of $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal B}(F(a),b)$ on $\mathcal C/T$ these form a matching family, hence glue to an isomorphism $\theta:F(a)\cong b$. Here unique gluing is precisely the sheaf condition of [def-weil-pbc-topos]; compatibility on common tests is equivalent to a matching family on the sieve generated by the covering, by defining its value through any factorization through a $u_i$. Thus each $F_T$ is essentially surjective. The argument also covers an empty covering: effectivity supplies $a$ and the sheaf axiom supplies the unique isomorphism.

The fibre functors are fully faithful by hypothesis and essentially surjective by the preceding construction. Apply [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-equivalence-criterion] to the given cartesian functor $F$. The base and fibre groupoids satisfy its size hypotheses by [def-weil-size-convention] and the item assumptions. It supplies a cartesian inverse over $\mathcal C$ with invertible unit and counit over identities, exactly the required equivalence.

Step 5 applies the new node; all its hypotheses hold (sizes, cartesian F, ff+ess surj fibres).
